our_argument_summary: Applying the dome's own kappa = 1.677 nT/uGal to the published 1999 eclipse magnetic perturbations predicts a 3-9 uGal contact-phase gravity pulse at Membach; the published SG record (Mansinha et al. 2001) shows a null at the 0.01-0.1 uGal floor, refuting the kappa prediction. The Chebychev-low-pass "the filter hid it" rescue is closed by three facts: (1) Mansinha was a dedicated eclipse-window search, not a generic decimated Level-3 product; (2) the IGETS Level-1 1-Hz raw archive is public and un-decimated, and no reanalysis finds the signal; (3) the rescue is self-defeating - the same filter family would also band-stop the Mohe valleys that anchor kappa's numerator, so either the null falsifies kappa or the numerator is itself a pipeline artifact.

holes_found.description: Verbatim duplicated paragraph introduced by the EXP-603 sweep. In the "What past SG data actually shows" paragraph, the three-sentence block beginning "The Mansinha 2001 reduction pipeline applies standard tidal-model and atmospheric-pressure-admittance corrections..." through "...the methodological caveat is addressed in What the dome could do below." appears TWICE consecutively (verbatim). The phrase "Mansinha 2001 reduction pipeline" only exists post-EXP-603 (Mansinha was substituted in by this EXP), so the duplication is a copy-paste artifact of the P5/P6 integrity sweep itself. Reader-visible in published prose - and editorial sloppiness in a section whose entire purpose is integrity is exactly the credibility the section cannot afford to leak.
holes_found.recommendation: Delete one copy of the three-sentence block (keep a single instance). The retained text should flow "...above the instrument noise floor of order 0.01-0.1 uGal at minute timescales. The Mansinha 2001 reduction pipeline applies... addressed in What the dome could do below. Crossley...". Mechanical dedup; no argument change. Recommend the integrity agent also scan part1, part4, part8b (the other EXP-603-touched sections) for the same copy-paste artifact.

holes_found.description: Chebychev-closure Fact 1 is now an argument-from-silence. With the fabricated 1-Hz inspection claim correctly withdrawn, Fact 1 reduces to "Nothing in that published reduction confines the search to a decimated Level-3 product" - i.e. the abstract does not RESTRICT the search to decimated data. A dome defender can reply that the abstract equally does not state the search was un-decimated, so Fact 1 no longer independently rules out the filter rescue; it leans on the absence of a restriction. The closure's actual weight now rests on Facts 2 (public Level-1 archive) and 3 (self-defeating against kappa's numerator).
holes_found.recommendation: Either (a) add a half-clause conceding Fact 1 is the weakest of the three and is corroborative rather than dispositive, then explicitly route the load to Facts 2-3; or (b) tighten Fact 1 to the verifiable core ("the published reduction reports examining the residual series for an eclipse-related change across the eclipse interval and finds none above ambient noise") and drop the stronger "nothing confines it to Level-3" inference. Honesty here mirrors the inline-withdrawal discipline the rest of the paragraph models.

holes_found.description: Fact 2 asserts that IGETS (GFZ Potsdam) "archives Level-1 SG records for Membach (BE001) across the 1999 eclipse window" without a dataset or station-inventory citation. IGETS was formed ~2015 succeeding GGP; a defender could question whether the specific Aug-1999 Membach 1-Hz Level-1 record is actually held/retrievable in IGETS. The claim is plausible (Membach SG operating since ~1995) but unanchored.
holes_found.recommendation: Add an IGETS station-inventory reference or the Membach (BE001) Level-1 dataset DOI to anchor the "anyone can pull the un-decimated record" claim. Not load-bearing on its own - Facts 1 and 3 stand without it - but a single citation removes the only factual soft target in the rebuilt closure.

stronger_arguments.description: Lead the Chebychev dissection with Fact 3 (the self-defeating-against-numerator dilemma) rather than ending on it. Fact 3 is the strongest leg - a clean either/or that needs no claim about what Mansinha did or did not decimate: either the filter passes the signal (Membach 1999 + Chinese 2009 nulls falsify kappa) or it stops the signal (the Mohe valleys anchoring kappa's numerator are themselves pipeline artifacts, and Yang & Wang 2002's no-anomaly reanalysis is the correct reading). Presenting the dilemma first would make Facts 1-2 corroborating detail rather than load-bearing, neutralizing the moderate hole above structurally.

kernel_of_truth.description: The Chebychev-low-pass rescue is not a strawman: standard SG processing genuinely applies low-pass/decimation filters when producing publication-quality Level-3 residuals, so the worry that a seconds-to-minutes contact-phase transient could be attenuated before publication is methodologically real (data/sections.json part6 6.14, "the most plausible-sounding" carve-out). The dome's instinct to attach the Membach null to a custodian-scientist name also has a real basis (EXP-603.json:kernel_of_truth - Michel Van Camp operates the Membach SG at ROB).
kernel_of_truth.why_it_doesnt_save_claim: The rescue is closed on the dome's own arithmetic: a 3-9 uGal predicted pulse is 30-900x the raw SG floor (data/sections.json part6 6.14), the un-decimated IGETS Level-1 record is public, and - decisively - the same filter family that would hide the eclipse pulse would also have stripped the minute-timescale Mohe "valleys" that supply kappa's numerator (Yang & Wang 2002, DOI 10.1023/A:1021119023985). Granting the kernel therefore costs the dome kappa itself, which is why the rebuilt WIN-013 "Refuted by Data" verdict is strengthened, not weakened, by the citation correction (EXP-603.json:why_kernel_doesnt_save_claim).
